optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Retail Store Operations

professionalSummary.text: Software Quality Engineer with 2 years of experience owning end-to-end quality for a store-task application on handheld devices in a regional grocery chain, including test suite maintenance, pilot-store testing, and release sign-off.
professionalSummary.witness: Responsibilities included suite maintenance, pilot-store rounds, readiness summaries and release notes for the store-task application over about two years, reporting to the store systems manager.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on handheld devices using Appium, adding offline-sync scenarios after a store outage.
experienceHighlights.witness: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet (Appium against the two device models in use), adding the offline-sync scenarios after a store outage.

experienceHighlights.text: Ran pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three stores before each release, recording outcomes and escalating blocking defects to the development lead.
experienceHighlights.witness: Ran the pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three pilot stores before each release, recording outcomes per scenario and escalating blocking defects to the development lead.

experienceHighlights.text: Prepared release readiness summaries for the store systems manager, who decided test scope with the development lead and provided release sign-off.
experienceHighlights.witness: Prepared the release readiness summary for the store systems manager, who decided the test scope with the development lead and gave the sign-off for the release to go to stores.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented known limitations and hand-over conditions in release notes for store operations, including device model requirements for features.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the release notes for store operations, listing known limitations (the task-photo feature needed the newer device model) and the hand-over items for the store support desk.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Appium test suite with offline-sync scenarios and pilot-store results sheet with device-farm run identifiers as verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the Appium suite's scenario list and one pilot-store round's results sheet, with the device-farm run identifiers as a verification trail.

skills.text: Appium, handheld device testing, release readiness coordination, defect escalation, documentation of limitations.
skills.witness: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet (Appium against the two device models in use)... Ran the pilot-store test rounds with store staff... Wrote the release notes for store operations, listing known limitations (the task-photo feature needed the newer device model)

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's direct experience with maintaining the test suite, running pilot tests, preparing readiness summaries, and documenting limitations. They do not establish the candidate's direct ownership of release sign-off (the store systems manager provided sign-off) or the candidate's coordination of release readiness with development and store operations (the store systems manager decided test scope with development lead).

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required to assess whether the candidate's role in release sign-off and coordination meets the requirement for direct ownership and accountability.

role.roleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Retail Store Operations

evidence.text: Responsibilities included suite maintenance, pilot-store rounds, readiness summaries and release notes for the store-task application over about two years, reporting to the store systems manager.
evidence.notes: Directly mentions responsibilities but not explicit ownership of sign-off.

evidence.text: Reference call with the former store systems manager: said the candidate 'knew the app better than anyone' and that she 'never had to overrule his readiness summary'; confirmed employment dates.
evidence.notes: Indirectly supports accountability but not explicit sign-off.

missingEvidence: Direct evidence of candidate holding sign-off before release

evidence.text: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet (Appium against the two device models in use), adding the offline-sync scenarios after a store outage.
evidence.notes: Explicitly states maintenance of test suite.

evidence.text: Work sample: the Appium suite's scenario list and one pilot-store round's results sheet, with the device-farm run identifiers as a verification trail.
evidence.notes: Supports test suite maintenance with work sample.

evidence.text: Ran the pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three pilot stores before each release, recording outcomes per scenario and escalating blocking defects to the development lead.
Work sample: the Appium suite's scenario list and one pilot-store round's results sheet, with the device-farm run identifiers as a verification trail.
evidence.notes: Supports pilot-store testing with work sample.

evidence.text: Prepared the release readiness summary for the store systems manager, who decided the test scope with the development lead and gave the sign-off for the release to go to stores.
evidence.notes: Candidate prepared summary but store systems manager decided scope and provided sign-off.

evidence.text: Reference call with the former store systems manager: said the candidate 'knew the app better than anyone' and that she 'never had to overrule his readiness summary'; confirmed employment dates.
evidence.notes: Indirectly supports coordination but not explicit coordination with development and store operations.

missingEvidence: Direct evidence of candidate coordinating release readiness with development lead and store operations

evidence.text: Wrote the release notes for store operations, listing known limitations (the task-photo feature needed the newer device model) and the hand-over items for the store support desk.
evidence.notes: Explicitly states documenting limitations and hand-over conditions.

supportedClaims.witness: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet (Appium against the two device models in use), adding the offline-sync scenarios after a store outage.

supportedClaims.witness: Ran the pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three pilot stores before each release, recording outcomes per scenario and escalating blocking defects to the development lead.

supportedClaims.claim: Documented known limitations and hand-over conditions in release notes for store operations, including device model requirements for features.
supportedClaims.witness: Wrote the release notes for store operations, listing known limitations (the task-photo feature needed the newer device model) and the hand-over items for the store support desk.

unsupportedClaims.claim: The candidate owned application quality end-to-end and held the sign-off before each release went to stores.
unsupportedClaims.reason: The store systems manager provided the sign-off, not the candidate.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Ask candidate to clarify their role in release sign-off and whether they had final authority.

unsupportedClaims.claim: The candidate coordinated release readiness with the development lead and store operations.
unsupportedClaims.reason: The store systems manager decided test scope with the development lead, and the candidate prepared the readiness summary but did not coordinate with store operations.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Ask candidate to describe their coordination with development lead and store operations during release readiness.

missingEvidenceGaps.gap: Candidate did not hold sign-off; store systems manager provided sign-off.
Candidate prepared readiness summary but did not coordinate with development lead and store operations.

interviewSignalRisks.text: Hiring manager pre-read: the candidate's CV cover note says he was 'accountable for store release quality end-to-end'; the head of store systems wants exactly that, so the packet must show what accountability he actually held.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify with candidate whether they held final sign-off authority or if the store systems manager did.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you describe your role in the release sign-off process, including whether you had final authority to approve releases before they went to stores?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Whether the candidate held sign-off authority or if the store systems manager did.

followUpQuestions.question: How did you coordinate release readiness with the development lead and store operations team?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Whether the candidate coordinated directly with both teams or if the store systems manager handled coordination.

humanReviewChecklist: Verify candidate's role in release sign-off authority
Confirm coordination with development lead and store operations
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The materials establish the candidate's direct experience with test suite maintenance, pilot-store testing, and documentation of limitations. However, they do not establish the candidate's direct ownership of release sign-off or coordination with development and store operations, which are critical for the role. Human review is required to assess these gaps.
limitations: The materials do not provide explicit evidence of the candidate's direct sign-off authority or coordination with store operations team.
